# Ordex

> Portable Bitcoin orders, verified before you act. Ordex is a non-custodial
> evidence and discovery layer for signed PSBT orders: it composes and
> verifies Bitcoin transactions, and it never signs, never holds or
> contributes funds, and never broadcasts on its own initiative.

Amounts are atomic integers carried as decimal strings, never floating point.
Paging is keyset, never offset. A public ask can be completed by anyone
holding the signed artifact, so it is never described as reserved.

The published guide lives at https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/ and
the implementation lives at https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex.

## Availability

The Bitcoin Universe capability snapshot records the Ordex marketplace surface
as feature-gated, in `psbt-routing-only` mode, behind the `ordex` feature gate.
Its recorded settlement policy is that Ordex never broadcasts or records a
completed settlement, and its recorded reason for not supporting a buy action
is that Ordex validates and routes PSBTs but explicitly does not fund, sign, or
broadcast settlement. Read every page below with that boundary in mind.

## Guides

- [Meet Ordex](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/): what a portable
  order carries, who the evidence is for, and what Ordex refuses to do.
- [Start safely](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/quickstart.html):
  five steps from discovering an order to completing it in your own wallet,
  plus the checks to make before you act.
- [How portable orders work](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/protocol-guide.html):
  protocol families, the lifecycle states a listing can hold, the three
  verification layers, and what a signature does and does not prove.
- [Architecture](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/architecture.html):
  the system map from wallet to gateway to Bitcoin Core, `ord`, Nostr relays,
  and compatible markets, with the trust boundary for each component.
- [API reference](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/api-reference.html):
  every route, parameter, response, and schema, generated from the OpenAPI
  contract at build time.
- [Get help](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/troubleshooting.html):
  what to do when a listing is pending, being spent, gone, not usable,
  withdrawn, or visible in one market but not another.

## Contract

- [The gateway API, explained](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/api.md):
  every route under `/api/ordex` and why it is shaped that way.
- [openapi.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/openapi.json):
  the OpenAPI 3.1 contract, field by field. Version 1.2 adds SafeOps, atomic
  swaps, realtime events, signed webhooks, collection provenance, Counterparty
  heritage, and offline signing, additively.
- [asyncapi.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/asyncapi.json):
  the AsyncAPI 3.0 streaming contract: SSE, WebSocket, and signed webhooks
  carrying the same ordex-event/v1 envelopes.
- [Order lifecycle](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/lifecycle.md):
  every reachable state and what a customer may do in each.
- [Completing a public ask](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/purchase.md):
  the two rules and the sat flow invariant that decide whether the asset
  reaches the buyer.
- [Offers v1](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/offers.md):
  item, collection, and trait offers with a funded Taproot output and a buyer
  recovery path.
- [Not burning the runes a purchase spends](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/runes.md):
  how the runestone assigns a rune balance, and why a cenotaph destroys runes
  in a transaction that Bitcoin itself accepts as valid.
- [Portable orders](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/interoperability.md):
  how an order enters and leaves a gateway, and the exact OpenOrdex kind 802
  event contract.
- [SafeOps v1](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/safeops.md):
  the executable operations desk: batch transfers, consolidations, RBF, CPFP,
  the execution shield, and post broadcast monitoring.
- [Atomic swaps and the OTC desk](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/swaps.md):
  maker intents, encrypted private links, and one transaction settlement where
  both sides move or nothing does.
- [Realtime events and signed webhooks](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/events.md):
  the ordex-event/v1 envelope, replay by cursor, and webhook signatures.
- [Collection provenance](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/collection-manifest.md):
  creator signed manifests, offline membership proofs, and revocation.
- [Counterparty heritage assets](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/counterparty-utxo-asset.md):
  UTXO attached assets, the attachment follow rule, and the readiness gate.
- [Cold signing and watch-only](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/spec/cold-signing.md):
  the expected transaction manifest, the nine refusals, and the signing
  stepper.
- [sdk/README.md](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/sdk/README.md):
  the typed TypeScript client generated from that contract.

## Conformance

- [conformance/purchase-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/purchase-vectors.json):
  the verdict a compatible verifier must reach for each named transaction
  shape.
- [conformance/rune-burn-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/rune-burn-vectors.json):
  the same for the rune burn rule, including the cases that burn.
- [conformance/safeops-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/safeops-vectors.json):
  plan and signed result verdicts, including the fail-closed inventory rules.
- [conformance/swap-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/swap-vectors.json):
  intent and acceptance verdicts, including the atomicity and sighash closure
  rules.
- [conformance/event-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/event-vectors.json):
  envelope and webhook signature verdicts.
- [conformance/collection-manifest-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/collection-manifest-vectors.json):
  manifest, revocation, and membership proof verdicts.
- [conformance/counterparty-asset-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/counterparty-asset-vectors.json):
  attachment record and attachment follow verdicts.
- [conformance/offline-signing-vectors.json](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/conformance/offline-signing-vectors.json):
  manifest and signed result comparison verdicts, one per refusal rule.
- [verifier/purchase.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/purchase.js):
  a dependency free reference verifier implementing the purchase rules, run by
  `npm test`.
- [verifier/runes.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/runes.js):
  the reference verifier for the rune burn rule, run by the same command.
- [verifier/safeops.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/safeops.js),
  [verifier/swaps.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/swaps.js),
  [verifier/events.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/events.js),
  [verifier/collection-manifest.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/collection-manifest.js),
  [verifier/counterparty-asset.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/counterparty-asset.js),
  and [verifier/offline-signing.js](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/verifier/offline-signing.js):
  the 1.2 reference verifiers, all run by the same command and all mirrored in
  the SDK.

## Repository

- [README.md](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/README.md):
  what the repository holds and how to build and test it.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/ordex/blob/main/SECURITY.md):
  the security policy and how to report a vulnerability.
- [docs.manifest.json](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/ordex/docs.manifest.json):
  the machine-readable documentation manifest for this repository.
